name: Tenuta San Guido Sassicaia 2013
text:
## Tenuta San Guido Sassicaia 2013

**The story.** Sassicaia comes from [Bolgheri](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Bolgheri,+Livorno,+Italy&t=k), on the Tuscan coast. Marchese Mario Incisa della Rocchetta gained the estate through his 1940 marriage to Clarice della Gherardesca, and in 1944 planted Cabernet cuttings on the Castiglioncello slope. You can see that hillside at [Castiglioncello di Bolgheri](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Castiglioncello+di+Bolgheri,+Livorno,+Italy&t=k).

From 1948 to 1967 the wine stayed a private family affair. The first official vintage was 1968. The wine is 85% Cabernet Sauvignon and 15% Cabernet Franc, with no Merlot. The Tenuta San Guido estate is shown at [Tenuta San Guido](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Tenuta+San+Guido,+Bolgheri,+Italy&t=k).

**The vintage.** The estate's cellar master described 2013 as slow and calm. An April frost thinned the crop, and a summer without extremes followed. Priscilla Incisa della Rocchetta called it a record vintage for Sassicaia.

**What the critics say.**
- **Wine Advocate:** Monica Larner gave 97 points in July 2016. She praised the balance and the seamless intensity. She also advised setting the wine aside for about ten more years.
- **James Suckling and Wine Enthusiast:** Both gave 98 points (November 2016 and March 2017). Suckling stressed the polished, chewy tannins. Wine Enthusiast liked the finesse and energy.
- **Falstaff:** Othmar Kiem gave 96 points on a 2019 tasting.
- **Wine Spectator and Vinous:** K&L's listing shows 95 from Wine Spectator and 92 from Vinous. That is the low end of the range. Vinous's earlier barrel tasting by Antonio Galloni was 93–96.
- **Natalie MacLean:** She gave 95/100 and a community score of 94 from five reviews. The CellarTracker figure of 93.9 is from your list. I did not open the CellarTracker page itself.
- **Jancis Robinson:** She has tasted this wine, but her score is behind a paywall, so I can't report it.

**Practical note.** The 2013 is at the start of its drinking window. Wine Enthusiast suggested drinking it between 2020 and 2038. Barrels Berry Bros. describes it as drinking beautifully now with a long way to go. My judgement is to decant for about an hour. Roast lamb or a rib roast suits it. Natalie MacLean named it her "Best Beef Wine."

**An aside on the soil.** The name means "place of many stones." Mario Incisa noticed that the stony soil resembled Graves in Bordeaux. Gravel drains quickly and forces vines to root deep.

**From the history books**
- 1944: first Cabernet cuttings planted on the estate. [Mario Incisa della Rocchetta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Mario+Incisa+della+Rocchetta&go=Go)
- 1968: the first commercial vintage, made with help from winemaker Giacomo Tachis. [Giacomo Tachis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Giacomo+Tachis&go=Go)
- 1978: Sassicaia won a Decanter blind tasting of Cabernets in London. The estate says the winner was the 1972 vintage. Decanter's own retrospective says the 1975. [Super Tuscan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Super+Tuscan&go=Go)
